subject: Private VPC deployment — next steps for VPC peering / PrivateLink
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@acmerobotics.com>; Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC deployment — next steps for VPC peering / PrivateLink

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our conversation: 

1) Deployment mode: you confirmed the requirement for a Private VPC (VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink) due to IP allowlist / data residency constraints. Hosted API is off the table; Dedicated could be an option later but Private VPC is the primary path.

2) Networking & connectivity items we need to validate:
   - VPC peering vs PrivateLink preference (you indicated peering preferred for direct routing)
   - CIDR ranges for peering and any overlapping addresses
   - Expected egress IPs / NAT gateway setup for outbound calls (so you can add to allowlists)
   - Transit gateway or shared services architecture if you have multiple accounts

3) Security/compliance asks: SOC 2 evidence and audit logs (we shared high-level doc in demo; attaching the connectivity guide and an example network diagram).

Next steps I propose:
- You share the contact for your networking/cloud infra lead and your preferred time for a short 30-min tech session (we suggest next week).
- I'll loop in Dev (networking engineer) from our infra team to map the peering/PrivateLink design and produce an IP allowlist and step-by-step guide.

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf (stub), redwood_vpc_connectivity_guide.pdf (stub)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@acmerobotics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — next steps for VPC peering / PrivateLink

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming:

- We want VPC peering if possible. Our security team prefers peering over PrivateLink for cross-account access (lower operational complexity for our architecture).
- I'll introduce you to our cloud infra lead, Jordan Lee (jordan.lee@acmerobotics.com), in a separate email — goal is a tech sync next Tue or Wed (Aug 25/26).
- CIDR ranges: currently our prod VPC is 10.10.0.0/16; we have a shared-services VPC at 10.20.0.0/16. No overlap with 10.0.0.0/8.
- For outbound IPs: we use NAT Gateways with Elastic IPs in each AZ. We can provide the EIPs once we finalize peering.

Can you have your networking lead prepare a simple list of the endpoints/ports and the expected source IP ranges for Redwood egress? That will help our security team create the allowlist quickly.

Appreciate the attachments — review underway. Talk soon.

— Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Robotics
alex.mercer@acmerobotics.com

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private VPC deployment — next steps for VPC peering / PrivateLink

Forwarding Alex's note — Acme Robotics (prod VPC 10.10.0.0/16) prefers VPC peering. They want a short tech session next Tue/Wed (25/26 Aug). Can you: 

- Draft a one-page connectivity checklist (peering steps, required route table updates, security group rules, recommended ports).
- Produce a preliminary list of Redwood egress IPs we expect to use (or guidance if we use a managed NAT range) so they can start the allowlist.
- Call out any limits (route table entries per VPC, cross-account IAM steps) we should surface in the tech call.

Attaching the network diagram and our connectivity guide for background.

Thanks — please mark urgent; they're in the procurement cycle and we want to avoid delays.

— Marissa

Quick notes from infra:

- For VPC peering we can provide a small set of egress IPs via our egress NAT (we typically allocate two Elastic IPs per region for HA). Expect the preliminary list to be 54.213.12.34 and 54.213.12.35 (subject to final provisioning).
- Ports: primarily HTTPS (443) outbound from our instances; if Acme wants to reach any management endpoints in our control plane we can open TCP 443 inbound from their peered CIDR.
- Route table: remember to add peering routes in both VPCs and verify propagation with your TGW if using transit.
- Cross-account IAM: we'll need a peering accept role or have them accept from their account; I'll prepare step-by-step notes.

I'll be on the tech call with Marissa tomorrow at 11:00 PT. Dev — can you have the checklist ready before then?

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Infrastructure
